standard.title: Protective behaviours and community resources
standard.description: refine protective behaviours and evaluate community resources to seek help for themselves and others
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have analysed and rehearsed protective behaviours and help-seeking strategies in online and offline situations (Y5-6). They have rehearsed protective behaviours but have not yet been expected to refine them through evaluation or to evaluate the quality and suitability of community resources.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students refine protective behaviours and evaluate community resources to seek help for themselves and others.

nodes.label: Identifying protective behaviours and when they apply
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a range of protective behaviours appropriate to different risk or help-seeking scenarios and explain the reasoning behind each.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two protective behaviours and explain the reasoning behind each in a specific scenario.
nodes.typical_width: Identify protective behaviours across a range of scenarios (mental health, online abuse, substance use, sexual health, bullying); explain why each behaviour protects safety or wellbeing in its specific context; distinguish proactive from reactive protective behaviours.
wider: Explore help-seeking scenarios young people may encounter — including situations linked to substance use, mental health, sexual health, safety and risk-taking — and identify which protective behaviours are most relevant to each

Investigate how emotions, gender norms and cultural expectations can affect a person's willingness to apply protective behaviours or seek help, and what this means for designing effective protective strategies

response_modes.reason: Protective behaviour application depends on having a range of behaviours available — students who only know one or two protective strategies will be unable to respond appropriately to diverse scenarios.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two protective behaviours
Explains the reasoning behind each behaviour in a specific scenario

nodes.label: Evaluating community resources for help-seeking
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and evaluate community resources available for help-seeking in a range of scenarios, assessing their accessibility, relevance and quality.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one community resource available for help-seeking in a specific scenario and give one reason for or against using it.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and evaluate resources across multiple domains (mental health, online safety, substance use, sexual health); assess accessibility, reliability and relevance for different scenarios; examine how support services like Kidshelpline and eSafety Commissioner operate.
wider: Analyse how online support services (Kidshelpline, eSafety Commissioner) are designed and evaluate their effectiveness for different types of situations young people encounter
Examine how gender norms and cultural expectations create barriers to help-seeking for different groups and evaluate which resources are designed to address these barriers
nodes.hinge_reason: Refining protective behaviours and evaluating resources are the twin demands of this descriptor — students who cannot evaluate resource quality cannot make informed help-seeking decisions for themselves or others. This evaluation capability is what separates knowing resources exist from being able to use them effectively.

response_modes.reason: Provide explicit evaluation criteria (accessibility, relevance, reliability, appropriateness for specific scenarios) before expecting evaluation judgements. Without criteria, resource evaluation defaults to surface-level familiarity.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one community resource available for help-seeking in a named scenario
Evaluates the resource against at least one criterion (accessibility, reliability or relevance)

nodes.label: Refining protective behaviours through scenario practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply and refine protective behaviours across a range of help-seeking scenarios, adjusting their approach based on the specific context and available resources.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply protective behaviours in at least one scenario and describe one way they refined their approach based on the specific context.
nodes.typical_width: Apply and refine protective behaviours across multiple scenario types; explain how bystanders play a role in ensuring safety; practise strategies for managing online abuse, substance pressure and mental health crises; connect protective behaviours to specific community resources.
wider: Explore strategies for dealing with online abuse and bullying when there is an imbalance of power — including grooming and image-based abuse — and practise reporting situations to appropriate authorities and through online tools
Collaborate with peers to suggest strategies for scenarios where a friend is being encouraged to use a substance, evaluating which strategies are most likely to be effective in a real peer context

response_modes.reason: Protective behaviour refinement requires repeated scenario practice — one rehearsal does not build the reliable, habitual responses that protective behaviour depends on in real situations.
Refined protective behaviours integrate knowledge of scenarios, resource evaluation and practical strategy — connecting resources to behaviours is essential so students can act, not just plan.

success_criteria: Applies protective behaviours in at least one scenario
Identifies at least one way to refine the approach for the specific context
Connects at least one protective behaviour to a specific community resource that would support it
